subject: Request: One-time 60d POC extension + discretionary credits for HelioWorks
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@helioworks.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: One-time 60d POC extension + discretionary credits for HelioWorks

Alex — quick context and an ask. HelioWorks is mid-POC and has run into two blockers that will meaningfully delay completion: (1) their procurement team needs SOC2 evidence and a completed SOW before they can spin up the dedicated test environment (est. 3–4 weeks), and (2) their security team wants an infra dive that’s taking longer than expected. They’re otherwise running good experiments (see attached short report).

Our standard PLG sandbox is 30 days + 20k free tokens. Helio is asking for a one-time 60-day extension and 75k in discretionary credits to finish the integration and complete their evaluation. The commercial upside here is non-trivial — Jordan estimates a >$400k ARR opportunity if the POC validates.

Ask: can we approve a one-time exception (60 days, up to 75k credits) contingent on a signed 12-mo commitment (discounted TCV clause) or an MSA signature within 45 days after the extension? I’ve attached the POC report and SOC2 outline.

If it helps, I can loop in Legal and Finance for a narrow term addendum and we can require that credits are only usable against production usage after contract signature. Looking for directional yes/no from Sales leadership and Aditya for exec-level signoff.

Thanks — Tessa

Attachments: Helio_POCTest_Report.pdf (summary), SOC2-outline.pdf (summary)

--
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

A few clarifications from our side: procurement needs the SOW (we attached comments) and we need sandbox throughput to match a 10k qps simulation later this month. If we can get the extension and credits we will prioritize the infra dive and commit to the 12‑month purchase window — the CFO is supportive but procurement timeline is the blocker.

I’ve copied Priya from procurement who will send the redlines we have for the SOW. We’d like to get this locked this week if possible so we don’t lose engineering momentum.

— Alex

Aditya — forwarding the details. Recommend approval with the following constraints: (1) cap credits at 75k tokens, (2) credits usable only for sandbox and infra testing, (3) credits expire if no signed MSA within 45 days after extension, and (4) require a 12‑month minimum commitment to unlock credits beyond 30k. This mitigates risk and keeps momentum.

If you’re comfortable, please provide exec sign-off so Legal can draft a short addendum and Finance can set the credit controls. Time sensitivity: procurement indicated they want this week to avoid re-prioritization of their engs.

— Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: One-time 60d POC extension + discretionary credits for HelioWorks

Folks — I’m approving a one-time exception with conditions. Approve: 60-day extension and up to 75k discretionary credits, with these terms: 
- Credits limited to sandbox/integration environments only (no production consumption).
- Credits expire if an MSA or signed SOW is not executed within 45 days of the extension end date.
- Customer must sign a 12-month commitment (minimum TCV threshold of $100k) to unlock credits beyond 30k — we can allow an initial 30k immediately and the remainder released upon signature.
- Finance to apply a spend-tag and usage guardrail; Legal to prepare a one-page addendum and a DocuSign envelope.

I expect Sales to push for signature aggressively; this is a tactical concession to protect pipeline while maintaining commercial guardrails. Jordan — please update forecast (HLW-2158) with these terms. Marissa — once Legal posts the addendum send it to Priya and Alex with a 72-hour turnaround request.

Aditya Rao
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
